body:
Founder real-time: 'why do we set up all 3 servers at once regardless if they are needed? because teardown is expensive? are they python servers or what?' Real answer: they're the real compiled C bin/brawlpit_server binary (not Python), and teardown/spawn is cheap (live-measured ~0.8s round trip including a real connect) -- it was never restructured after the loop was written to train roles sequentially, meaning 2 of every 3 roles' servers sat fully idle (a full CPU core each) at any instant, a real waste that got worse with --num-envs. Restructured: each role's own servers now spawn right before its training chunk and tear down right after; paused (disabled-checkpoint) roles spawn nothing at all; models persist across generations via lazy construction + model.set_env(). Live-verified: only 1 server process running at a time during a real training run (confirmed via ps aux), and measured throughput improved (18.8 steps/sec vs the prior 11.3 baseline) purely from eliminating idle-server CPU contention. 129/129 tests pass.

⚓ ☃
title: S441: only spawn a role's own servers while it's actively training, not all 3 for the whole run
